reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, mu any probability measure on E, and S=NNReal times E times Nat times E^Nat. Let a:S to R be measurable and positive at every state, and let B be any nonnegative threshold. For s=(b,u,k,h), define F(s,y)=(b+1/a(s),(b*u+y/a(s))/(b+1/a(s)),k+1,h_y), with h_y(0)=y and h_y(m+1)=h(m). Vector division means reciprocal scalar multiplication and the first coordinate remains NNReal.
There exist Markov kernels T,H:S to E with T(s) equal to mu normalized by the density exp(-b*norm(x-u)^2/2) and H(s) equal to its convolution with the centered isotropic Gaussian of standard deviation sqrt(a(s)). After these same T,H are fixed, for every Markov Q,L:S to E there exist Markov P:S to S and Markov R_n:S to E, with P(s)=dirac s if B<=b and the F(s,.) pushforward of Q(s) otherwise. R_0=L, and R_(n+1)(s)=L(s) if B<=b and the bind of Q(s) with y mapped to R_n(F(s,y)) otherwise. Equality with the threshold belongs to the stopped branch.
Define e(s)=0 if B<=b and KL(Q(s)||H(s)) otherwise, and t(s)=KL(L(s)||T(s)). Both are measurable extended-nonnegative-real functions. For every n and every initial s, KL(R_n(s)||T(s)) <= sum over 0<=j<n of integral e(x) under P^j(s), plus integral t(x) under P^n(s). P^0 is the identity kernel. The terminal term is integrated under the time-n state law, not evaluated at the initial state. The left reference law is T(s) at the initial state. All KL values, sums and nonnegative integrals may be infinity; no absolute continuity or finite entropy assumption is present. For n=0 the sum is empty and the conclusion is KL(L(s)||T(s))<=t(s).
Quantifiers are all E,mu,a with the displayed structures and assumptions, then all B, then existence of T,H, then all Markov Q,L, then existence of P and the entire sequence R_n, then all n,s. P,R may depend on Q,L; T,H are chosen before them. No approximation quality of Q,L, bounded stopping time or threshold-hitting conclusion is stated.
